era: La Niña Fades & El Niño Watch Issued (Jan–May 2026)

events.title: La Niña Still Present Across Equatorial Pacific
events.detail: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center reported equatorial sea-surface temperatures below average across the east-central and eastern Pacific during the January-February-March period, with atmospheric anomalies consistent with a weak, waning La Niña.

events.title: 2025–26 La Niña Weakens Below Threshold
events.detail: The 2025-26 La Niña event weakened below La Niña thresholds in February-March 2026 as equatorial Pacific temperatures rebounded toward neutral, setting the stage for a rapid swing toward El Niño later in the year.

events.title: NOAA Forecast Shows Hard Turn Toward El Niño
events.detail: NOAA's March 2026 ENSO probability update showed a sharp swing from the February forecast, projecting more than 60% probability of El Niño onset by mid-summer 2026 — an unusually fast transition out of La Niña.

events.title: Super Typhoon Sinlaku Strikes Northern Mariana Islands
events.detail: Sinlaku became the 2026 Pacific typhoon season's first typhoon on April 10 and intensified into the season's first Category 5 super typhoon on April 12, making a direct pass through the Northern Mariana Islands with sustained winds up to 215 km/h — an unusually early and intense signal for the developing El Niño season.

events.title: WMO Update Shows Rising El Niño Probability
events.detail: The WMO's El Niño/La Niña Update for May 2026 showed forecast probabilities for El Niño conditions reaching 80% for June-August 2026, with ENSO-neutral odds falling to just 20%, and El Niño remaining dominant near or above 90% probability through the September-November window.

events.title: Record Pre-Monsoon Heatwave Kills Dozens Across South Asia
events.detail: A 15-day pre-monsoon heatwave from April 15-29 pushed daily maximum temperatures above 46°C in numerous Indian and Pakistani cities, killing at least 37 people in India and 10 in Karachi, Pakistan. World Weather Attribution found human-caused climate change made the heatwave roughly three times more likely.

events.title: Panama Canal Authority Pre-Emptively Trims Draft Limits
events.detail: The Panama Canal Authority issued an advisory trimming the maximum draft for Neopanamax locks from 50 feet to 49.5 feet, effective July 3 — a modest, precautionary step reflecting healthier starting lake levels than during the severe 2023-24 El Niño drought that had forced daily transits down to 24 vessels.

events.title: NOAA Upgrades El Niño Watch to Advisory
events.detail: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center formally upgraded its ENSO alert status from El Niño Watch to El Niño Advisory, confirming El Niño conditions were present with the Niño 3.4 SST anomaly at approximately +0.7°C and a strong subsurface warm pool signaling continued intensification.

events.title: Niño 3.4 Anomaly Jumps to +1.8°C
events.detail: By the last week of June, the Niño 3.4 monitoring region was running about +1.8°C above the 1991-2020 baseline — a rapid jump from the +0.7°C reading at the June 11 advisory upgrade, confirming an unusually fast rate of intensification.

events.title: India's Monsoon Opens With 40% Rainfall Deficit
events.detail: India's southwest monsoon opened June 2026 with a steep 40% rainfall deficit nationally, with the northwest region recording a 91% shortfall and central India 49% below average. Kharif planting covered only 35 million hectares versus 44.3 million hectares at the same point in 2025.

events.title: Peru Extends Anchovy Fishing Suspension Again
events.detail: Peru's fisheries authority extended its suspension of anchovy fishing in the North-Central zone beyond the initial June 10 deadline as warm coastal waters continued to disperse the stock. May 2026 anchovy landings for fishmeal and fish oil had already collapsed 97.6% year-over-year, from 1.33 million to just 31,771 tons.

events.title: Kenya Activates National Disaster Plan Ahead of El Niño Rains
events.detail: Kenya's weather service confirmed an 80-82% likelihood that El Niño would persist through the year and activated the national disaster contingency plan ahead of anticipated heavier October-December short rains, following a biphasic pattern of drought June-September followed by potential deluge.

events.title: Somalia Faces 60% Chance of Above-Average Rainfall
events.detail: FEWS NET assessed a 60% chance of above-average rainfall across southern and southwestern Somalia for the upcoming rainy season, raising flood risk on top of an existing crisis that has left 4.8 million people in need of urgent humanitarian aid amid overlapping drought and displacement.

era: Strong El Niño Confirmed & Cascading Impacts (July 2026)

events.title: WMO: Strong El Niño Expected to Intensify Through October
events.detail: WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said the world needed to prepare for a potentially strong El Niño event that would exacerbate drought, heavy rainfall, and heatwave risk both on land and in the ocean, noting the 2023-24 event was among the five strongest on record and helped drive 2024's record global temperatures.

events.title: Panama Canal Draft Limit Cut Takes Effect
events.detail: The Panama Canal Authority's trimmed 49.5-foot draft limit for Neopanamax locks took effect, a precautionary measure well short of the sub-44-foot restrictions and 24-vessel daily caps imposed during the severe 2023-24 El Niño drought.

events.title: Forecasters Warn Super El Niño Could Exceed Earlier Projections
events.detail: CNN reported that meteorologists who had already flagged this El Niño as intense were revising projections upward, citing faster-than-expected Niño 3.4 warming and subsurface heat content running ahead of the 1997-98 and 2015-16 reference events at the same point in their evolution.

events.title: Landslides and Flooding Kill 15 in Cox's Bazar Refugee Camps
events.detail: Landslides and flooding in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar Rohingya refugee camps killed at least 15 people and displaced more than 10,000 since the start of July 2026, as El Niño-linked rainfall anomalies compounded the camps' existing vulnerability to slope failure.

events.title: Record El Niño Threatens to Unleash Floods Across East Africa and Asia
events.detail: Al Jazeera reported the intensifying El Niño pattern threatened severe flooding, disease outbreaks, and heatwaves across East Africa and Asia in the coming weeks, with Kenya, Uganda, Somalia, Bangladesh, Pakistan, and Afghanistan named among the most exposed countries.

events.title: Peru's GDP Growth Hits 2026 Low as Fisheries Collapse Drags Output
events.detail: Peru's fisheries collapse dragged national GDP growth to its lowest rate of 2026 at 1.80% in May, as the anchovy season's near-total suspension cut fishmeal and fish oil exports to roughly $280 million — about one-fifth of the $1.4 billion a normal season generates.

events.title: Cocoa Prices Cross $5,000/Tonne on El Niño Supply Fears
events.detail: Cocoa futures crossed $5,000 a tonne as the developing El Niño threatened to hamper West Africa's October main crop with dry, hot conditions; Citi flagged $6,000 as a possible target, noting every strong El Niño in the past 55 years has reduced global cocoa production. West Africa supplies nearly 70% of the global crop.

events.title: Indonesia Fire Hotspots Exceed Prior El Niño Years
events.detail: Satellite fire-monitoring platform FireWatch recorded more than 96,000 fire hotspots across Indonesia by late July 2026 — exceeding totals recorded at the same point in the 2015, 2019, and 2023 El Niño years — as El Niño and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole suppressed rainfall across Sumatra and Kalimantan.

events.title: Munich Re: H1 2026 Catastrophe Losses Below Average, El Niño Risk Looms
events.detail: Munich Re pegged global H1 2026 insured catastrophe losses at $46 billion, 28% below the 10-year average, but warned that intensifying El Niño conditions and extreme European heat could heighten losses later in the year as drought and wildfire risk climbs.

events.title: UN Warns Powerful El Niño Will Intensify Heat on 'a Planet Already on Fire'
events.detail: The WMO warned that the strengthening El Niño would intensify heat extremes on what it called a planet already on fire, with Secretary-General Celeste Saulo stressing that forecasts alone do not prevent hazards — only anticipatory action by governments and communities does.

events.title: Berkeley Earth: Odds of 2026 as Hottest Year Jump to 69%
events.detail: Berkeley Earth raised the odds of 2026 becoming the hottest year on record from 12% in July to 69% in August, as the unusually powerful El Niño that began in June pushed the first half of 2026 to the third-warmest start to a year on record at roughly 1.4°C above pre-industrial levels.

events.title: Tropical Sea Snakes Reach California as El Niño Depletes Pacific Food Web
events.detail: NASA's PACE satellite documented tropical sea snakes appearing off the California coast as El Niño-driven warming disrupted the Pacific food web, echoing marine species displacement patterns seen during the 1997-98 and 2015-16 Super El Niño events.

events.title: Indonesian Haze Reaches Singapore and Malaysia
events.detail: Wildfire haze from Sumatra and Kalimantan drifted into Singapore and Malaysia as El Niño-suppressed rainfall disabled Indonesia's cloud-seeding mitigation efforts; regional watchdog SIIA issued a rare Red haze alert covering Indonesia, Singapore, Malaysia, and Brunei, flagging August-September as the highest-risk window.

events.title: NOAA CPC: 69% Chance of Historic El Niño Event
events.detail: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center reported a 69% chance that the October-December 2026 El Niño event would exceed the strength of every event in the historical record dating back to 1950, based on Niño 3.4 anomalies and subsurface heat content tracking above the 1997-98 and 2015-16 reference events.

events.title: Models Converge on November 2026–January 2027 Peak
events.detail: 23 of 26 forecast models project the El Niño will peak during October-December 2026 at very strong intensity (Niño 3.4 ≥ +2.0°C), with roughly 63% probability of a very strong (Super) El Niño peaking between November 2026 and January 2027 — among the largest events in the 1950-present record.

events.title: Indonesia Projects Drought Persisting Into Early 2027
events.detail: Indonesia's BMKG meteorology agency projected El Niño-driven drought and fire risk would persist into early 2027 across Java, Sumatra, and Kalimantan, with 2026 wildfire risk accumulating faster than during the 2015, 2019, and 2023 El Niño cycles.

events.title: UK Met Office: El Niño Set to Be Strongest in Living Memory
events.detail: The UK Met Office said the developing El Niño is on track to be the most intense in over a century, with equatorial Pacific sea-surface temperatures already more than 2°C above normal and forecast to exceed 3°C later in 2026. Head of long-range forecasting Prof Adam Scaife called it 'an unprecedented event,' while climate scientist Dr Nick Dunstone said 2027 is 'very likely' to replace 2024 as the warmest year on record.

events.title: WMO: 2027 Likely to Set New Global Temperature Record
events.detail: The WMO's annual decadal climate update projected an 86% chance that at least one year between 2026 and 2030 will surpass 2024 as the warmest year on record, with lead author Leon Hermanson noting the developing El Niño increases the chances of 2027 being the next record-breaking year, potentially reaching 1.7°C above pre-industrial levels.
